newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea soon to lower money market rate -official.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea soon to lower money market rate -official.

text.p: South Korea will soon lower money market rates by one to two percent to help the corporate sector, an official at the ruling New Korea Party said on Wednesday.
"One way or another, the market rate is soon to be cut as senior officials at the party and government economic planners have agreed to lower interest rates," the official said.
The official said he expected yields on benchmark corporate bonds to fall to 10 percent from 12 percent currently.
"But they are still discussing with the central bank ways to lower the rates," he added.
He said officials discussed at the meeting a cut in reserve requirements for banks, money supply flexibility and a relaxation of rules on overseas borrowings.
But he declined to comment on market rumours that the central bank would announce a cut in the reserve ratio on October 23.
"The move aims at boosting corporate international competitivenss by offering cheaper funds," the official said.
The Seoul stock market has risen on anticipation that the government would announce the cut in the ratio following Wednesday's meeting, chaired by President Kim Young-sam.

The government released earlier today measures to boost its sagging economy, including slashing domestic steel prices and opening power production to private sector competition. But the rate cut was not included in the package.
